L16: > Abstract:Let $f \geq 0$ be operator monotone on $[0, \infty)$. In this paper we prove that for any unitarily-invariant norm $|||-|||$ on $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ and matrices $A, B, X \in M_n(\mathbb{C})$ with $A, B \geq 0$ and $|||X||| \leq 1$, \[|||f(A)X-Xf(B)||| \leq C f(|||AX-XB|||)\] for $C < 1.01975$. We do this by reducing this inequality to a function approximation problem and we choose approximate minimizers.
L17: This is much progress toward the conjecturally optimal value of $C=1$ which is known only in the case of the Hilbert-Schmidt norm. When $|||-|||$ is the the operator norm $||-||$, we obtain a great reduction of the previously known estimate of $C = 1.25$.
L18: > We further prove that for $|||X||| \leq 1$, \[|||A^{1/2}X-XB^{1/2}||| \leq 1.00891 |||AX-XB|||.\] This is a great improvement toward the conjecture of G. Pedersen that this inequality for $|||-|||$ being the operator norm holds with $C = 1$.
L19: > We discuss other related inequalities, including some sharp commutator inequalities. We also prove a sharp equivalence inequality between the operator modulus of continuity and the commutator modulus of continuity for continuous functions on $\mathbb{R}$.

L31: # Operator space theory from the maximal viewpoint
L32: 
L33: ORCID 0000-0002-3091-2049
L34: 
L35: by Affiliation: Gilles Pisier Affiliation: Sorbonne Université and Texas A&M University Affiliation: and Affiliation: Jean Roydor Affiliation: Sorbonne Université
L36: ###### Abstract
L37: We initiate a theory of “operator spaces” (in other words subspaces of $C^{*}$-algebras) with an emphasis on the maximal tensor product. The natural morphisms become the maximally bounded maps instead of the completely bounded ones. With this new looking glass we first examine various issues : lifting and extension properties, local reflexivity, inner derivations, similarity problems.
L38: This first part is semi-expository while the second one focuses on the class of von Neumann algebras $M$ such that any completely bounded unital homomorphism on a $C^{*}$-algebra with values in $M$ is maximally bounded (or equivalently is similar to a $*$-homomorphism via a similarity belonging to $M$). We show that this holds if and only if $M$ is the direct sum of a finite von Neumann algebra and an injective one.
